title: Floquet Dressing and Bath Spectral Effects on the Geometric Phase of a Driven Dissipative Qubit
abstract: Building on recent work by Wang et al. on the dissipative geometric phase (GP) in the spin-boson model (SBM), the GP dynamics of a periodically driven symmetric SBM are investigated using the numerically exact process-tensor time-evolving matrix product operator (PT-TEMPO) method. A symmetric two-level system subjected to a longitudinal monochromatic drive along the same system coordinate that couples to an Ohmic bosonic environment exhibits rich GP dynamics arising from the interplay between driving and dissipation. To isolate cooperative drive-bath effects, a non-additive GP contribution is introduced that separates the driven dissipative response from its driven-unitary and undriven-dissipative components. Periodic driving is found to either suppress or enhance bath-induced GP deformation depending on the interplay between drive and bath timescales. These trends are interpreted through Floquet spectral steering, whereby the drive redistributes the coherent dynamics among quasienergy sidebands whose transition frequencies and Fourier-resolved system-bath matrix elements determine their coupling to the environmental spectrum. Floquet analysis shows that the dominant dissipative pathways are governed jointly by Floquet matrix-element weights and bath spectral overlap, rather than by either alone. These results connect Floquet engineering, quantum dissipation, and GP dynamics and establish periodic driving as a means of controlling the GP of open quantum systems (OQSs).
summary: This paper analyzes the geometric phase dynamics of a driven, dissipative qubit using advanced numerical techniques. It demonstrates that periodic driving allows for active control over how the environment deforms the quantum phase. The findings establish a crucial link between Floquet engineering, quantum dissipation, and the control of open quantum system dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the interplay between periodic driving (Floquet dressing) and environmental dissipation affects the geometric phase (GP) accumulated by a driven qubit.
main_result: Periodic driving offers a mechanism to control the dissipative geometric phase, as the resulting dissipation pathways depend jointly on Floquet matrix-element weights and the bath spectral overlap.
method: The study employs the numerically exact Process-Tensor Time-Evolving Matrix Product Operator (PT-TEMPO) method combined with Floquet theory to analyze the reduced density matrix dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a symmetric two-level system (qubit) modeled by the Spin-Boson Model (SBM), subjected to a longitudinal monochromatic drive and coupled to an Ohmic bosonic environment.
key_observables: Geometric Phase (GP), non-additive GP contribution ($\delta\gamma_D$), and the purity/Bloch vector trajectory of the reduced density matrix.
important_parameters: Drive amplitude ($A$), drive frequency ($\Omega$), and the characteristic bath spectral density parameters ($\alpha, \omega_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis avoids assuming weak coupling or Markovian dynamics, using the PT-TEMPO method for accuracy.
figures_summary: Figures compare the strengths of three coupling terms—Floquet matrix-element weights, bath spectral density, and their product—across different drive frequency regimes to determine the conditions for strong dissipation.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure introducing the model, reviewing the theoretical framework (including GP and Floquet theory), presenting numerical results analyzing the drive-bath interplay, and concluding with the implications for quantum control.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the control of quantum coherence (GP) in realistic, open quantum systems by explicitly incorporating the effects of time-periodic driving, which is a major topic in modern quantum physics.

With increasing drive ampli- tude, higher-order Floquet sectors become increasingly mixed, giving rise to additional avoided crossings and a progressively richer quasienergy structure.
